risks.text: A module root may hold only index/route/service/repo/types/schema; any other file goes in libs/ behind libs/index.ts, and repos and services may not import upward. structure.test.ts enforces it, and the production pipeline failed on a catalog file left in the module root - apps/server/test/structure.test.ts:67 (history 4c4eaab)

Upload and webhook body limits read Content-Length first and then the whole body: a chunked request (no header) is fully in memory before the check. models/body.ts and workflows/route.ts recheck the size after reading, so the limit holds; the inbound webhook at webhooks/route.ts:194 does not, so a chunked body of any size is read in full - apps/server/src/modules/webhooks/route.ts:194

signInWithPassword returns before bcrypt runs when the email is unknown or the user is not native, so an unknown account answers faster than a wrong password; the bcrypt 72-byte limit is enforced only in the sign-up schema, not in verifyPassword - apps/server/src/services/user.service.ts:107

rules.rule: A PR has at most one migration, started from db:generate; a migration that was merged or deployed is never edited or deleted, a new one is added instead.
rules.why: A database may already have run it, so an edit leaves that database and the snapshot different from the code.

checks.why: regenerates the migration and snapshot from the schema

rules.rule: Every customer table is read and written scoped by workspace_id and environment_id; a Drizzle relation does not scope a query, so the query must still filter by both.
rules.why: One customer, or a sandbox, would read or change the data of another.

rules.rule: Event and entity properties, action and entity definitions and the decision context use json, not jsonb.
rules.why: jsonb sorts object keys and the key order changes the model answers (14 of 100 evaluation decisions).

rules.rule: Only admins change client settings, through every route: the session PUT checks the admin role and the API-key PUT /client-settings is reachable only with a secret key; keep public keys out of the allowed list in api-auth.
rules.why: A public key sits in a web page, so anyone reading it could overwrite the settings of the environment.

rules.rule: A password is at most 72 bytes at sign-up, checked by the auth schema before bcrypt.
rules.why: bcrypt reads only the first 72 bytes, so two longer passwords sharing them would both sign in.

rules.rule: The decision context keeps plain-object insertion order and no code sorts its keys; a change to the context, questions or policy is measured with the evaluation suite.
rules.why: Key order alone changed 14 of 100 decisions, so customers would see different answers.

rules.rule: Run pnpm eval:accept only after an improvement that you can explain.
rules.why: accepted.json is the regression gate, so accepting a worse result hides a real loss in catch rate.

rules.rule: Webhook verification signs id.timestamp.rawbody with HMAC-SHA-256, rejects timestamps more than 300 seconds off and accepts several secrets, the same in the TypeScript and Python SDKs.
rules.why: Forged or replayed deliveries would pass, or secret rotation would drop real ones, for customers on either language.

rules.rule: Pages for customers carry no pnpm commands, localhost, repo paths or server settings; those go in docs/deployment/.
rules.why: Customers of kairos.finic.ai would see server internals, and the docs build warns.

checks.why: prints a warning for each customer page that breaks this

rules.rule: Edit templates/events/*.json and run pnpm docs:events; do not edit docs/templates/events/*.md by hand.
rules.why: A core test fails when a page differs from its JSON file.

checks.why: rewrites the pages from the JSON files
